blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights Helios as a groundbreaking reference architecture for next-generation distributed big-data processing systems at Microsoft, capturing around a quadrillion events and indexing 16 trillion search keys daily. The paper argues for a shift from traditional cloud-centric architectures to a federated model that 'embraces the edge,' integrating end devices, edge computing, and cloud into a unified data processing platform. Colyer emphasizes the need for this architecture due to growing data volume, velocity, and privacy concerns, as well as latency limitations of centralized systems. The key insight is the concept of 'function spreading' and 'data spreading,' where computation and data are distributed across layers to minimize data movement and improve efficiency. The architecture also aims to unify batch and online processing, reducing the need for duplicated logic and enabling real-time analytics.
paper_title: Helios: Hyperscale Indexing for the Cloud & Edge
paper_abstract: Helios is a distributed, highly-scalable system used at Microsoft for flexible ingestion, indexing, and aggregation of large streams of real-time data that is designed to plug into relational engines. The system collects close to a quadrillion events indexing approximately 16 trillion search keys per day from hundreds of thousands of machines across tens of data centers around the world. Helios use cases within Microsoft include debugging/diagnostics in both public and government clouds, workload characterization, cluster health monitoring, deriving business insights and performing impact analysis of incidents in other large-scale systems such as Azure Data Lake and Cosmos. Helios also serves as a reference blueprint for other large-scale systems within Microsoft. We present the simple data model behind Helios, which offers great flexibility and control over costs, and enables the system to asynchronously index massive streams of data. We also present our experiences in building and operating Helios over the last five years at Microsoft. PVLDB Reference Format: Rahul Potharaju, Terry Kim, Wentao Wu, Vidip Acharya, Steve Suh, Andrew Fogarty, Apoorve Dave, Sinduja Ramanujam, Tomas Talius, Lev Novik, Raghu Ramakrishnan. Helios: Hyperscale Indexing for the Cloud & Edge. PVLDB, 13(12): 3231-3244, 2020. DOI: https://doi.org/10.14778/3415478.3415547
